[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Rotation Matching** [CF 1365C · Rotation Matching](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1365/C){rating="1400"}

Two shifts, one degree of freedom. Shifting $a$ by $s_1$ and $b$ by $s_2$ lines up the same pairs as keeping $a$ fixed and shifting $b$ by $k = s_2 - s_1 \pmod n$, so only $n$ relative rotations exist.

Now think per value instead of per rotation. A value $v$ sits at $\text{pos}_a(v)$ in $a$ and $\text{pos}_b(v)$ in $b$. Rotating $b$ right by $k$ moves it to $(\text{pos}_b(v) + k) \bmod n$, so $v$ matches exactly when
$$k \equiv \text{pos}_a(v) - \text{pos}_b(v) \pmod n.$$
Each value casts one vote for the rotation that matches it; the answer is the **largest vote count**. $n$ values, one histogram, $O(n)$.

[Solved in full in @sec-part-p5-b.]{.card-link}

:::
